title: Service Late-Fee History Add-On to the Fleet Order Deposit Rate
content:
**Vehicle Purchase Agreements, Fleet Vehicle Purchase Agreement: late-history rate on the order deposit**

A buyer whose service ledger shows late fees adds a late-history rate to the order deposit rate. The record read is the late fees charged on the buyer's service ledger with Service Accounts and Repair Orders.

| Service late fees charged in the last 24 whole months before the handling date | Late-history rate added |
|---|---|
| two or more | **5 percent (0.05)** |
| exactly one | **2.5 percent (0.025)** |
| none | nothing |

A service late fee falls in the last 24 whole months when fewer than 24 whole calendar months have passed from its ledger date to the handling date. A month is whole once the same day of the month is reached.

**Basis Q&A**
- *Is a late fee charged exactly 24 whole months before the handling date counted?* No. Once 24 whole months have passed, the fee falls outside the window. A fee dated one day later in the calendar falls inside it.
- *Does the amount of the service late fees matter?* No. Only the number of service late fees charged in the window counts.
- *Hypothetical:* the ledger shows three service late fees, one 30 months ago and two within the last year. Two fall in the window, so the late-history rate added is 5 percent.
